summary: Diana Reeves led the Q2 executive business review with Tom Bradley (engineering), James Mitchell (sales), Brian Cho (support) and Megan Lawson (product). Net revenue retention fell from 106% to 94%, driven by the Ironworks churn and free year-one Comply discounts, while new logos rose with Keystone's Detect add-on, Brightpath's two-year renewal and Larkspur Financial signing on Keystone's reference. Tom reported 100% Detect availability since March and an internal heartbeat live since May 29, but acknowledged at least six customer incidents caused by remediation work, now subject to staged rollout and restore verification. Brian reported support volume 22% above Q1 and a backlog reduced from 41 to 14 aged cases. Megan confirmed the three Comply tiers were approved on June 20 and overage credits issued, and that Protect multi-region replication has slipped to early Q4. Northstar's Detect renewal is at risk. Q3 priorities are the customer pipeline health panel, two support hires, the Professional plus Protect bundle, and Identity role inheritance.
actionItems: Tom Bradley: Ship the customer-facing pipeline health panel and schedule quarterly chaos game days in Q3
Brian Cho: Open requisitions for two support engineers
James Mitchell: Launch the Comply Professional plus Protect bundle once the scheduler rollout reaches 100%
